sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation — Constraints
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 official documentation, version path pinned.
sources.locator: §5.5 lines 92–101 (CHECK null/cross-row and immutability caveats); §5.5.6 lines 377–387 (EXCLUDE semantics).
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the PostgreSQL 18 constraints documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CHECK constraints cannot guarantee conditions over other rows/tables; UNIQUE, EXCLUDE, or FOREIGN KEY are suggested where applicable. EXCLUDE enforces only the declared operators over specified columns/expressions; schema/operator/index design matters.
sources.applicability: Confirms the draft's cross-row limitation and its caveat that interval exclusion is conditional and incomplete for qualification/dependency rules.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation — SET TRANSACTION
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 official documentation, version path pinned.
sources.locator: Lines 38–53: READ COMMITTED default; SERIALIZABLE visibility and serialization_failure rollback; isolation level must be set before first query/write.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the PostgreSQL 18 transaction documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: SERIALIZABLE detects concurrent patterns that cannot correspond to serial execution by aborting one transaction; callers need retry behavior. It does not itself supply roster rules.
sources.applicability: Confirms the draft correctly treats serializable transactions as a candidate mechanism with application retry handling, not as a complete business validator.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation — Row Security Policies
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 official documentation, version path pinned.
sources.locator: §5.9 lines 20–27: policies absent by default; after enablement no policy means default-deny; table owner normally bypasses; superuser/BYPASSRLS always bypass.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read PostgreSQL 18 row-security documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: RLS is not enabled by default. Policy default-deny applies only after enablement. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY can subject table owners; superusers and BYPASSRLS always bypass.
sources.applicability: Confirms the investigator's statement and supports keeping database role testing separate from sync filtering and application authorization.

sources.title: PNG Specification, Second Edition

sources.locator: Sections on color space/significant chunks (iCCP, sRGB, gAMA/cHRM), transparency/alpha representation, and decoder recommendations.

sources.title: Sharp input metadata API
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current Sharp documentation consulted with v0.35.5 release identified separately.
sources.locator: metadata() API; dimensions/orientation/pages/profile fields.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official API page and read metadata() description.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Metadata is read from the file header without decoding compressed pixels; width/height do not account for EXIF orientation.
sources.applicability: Useful intake preflight; header-only inspection is not proof dimensions are trustworthy or decode is safe.

sources.title: Sharp constructor and limits
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current Sharp documentation consulted with v0.35.5 release identified separately.
sources.locator: Constructor options failOn and limitInputPixels.
sources.observed_operation: Found and opened official constructor option descriptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: failOn defaults to warning; invalid metadata always aborts. limitInputPixels defaults to 268402689 and assumes metadata dimensions can be trusted; false/zero removes the limit.
sources.applicability: Shows a configurable decoder guard and its trust boundary; set a product limit and worker ceilings.

sources.title: Sharp image operations
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current Sharp documentation consulted with v0.35.5 release identified separately.
sources.locator: rotate() and autoOrient() sections.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official operation documentation and read rotation ordering/orientation behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: autoOrient reads EXIF Orientation and removes the tag; orientation carried elsewhere such as XMP is not handled. Order matters for rotate/resize/extract; multipage limitations apply.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit single orientation stage and fixture needs; not a guarantee for every decoder/format.

sources.title: Sharp output, profiles and metadata
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current Sharp documentation consulted with v0.35.5 release identified separately.
sources.locator: keepIccProfile(), withIccProfile(), keepMetadata(), withMetadata(); JPEG defaults.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official API page and read output profile/metadata policy descriptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Without keepMetadata, output converts to sRGB and strips metadata including ICC; keepMetadata retains EXIF, ICC, XMP and IPTC; withMetadata keeps most descriptive metadata and adds sRGB ICC if appropriate. JPEG defaults include quality 80 and 4:2:0 chroma subsampling.
sources.applicability: Concrete default/privacy/color behavior to override explicitly per output role.

sources.title: Pillow ImageOps 12.3.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: Pillow 12.3.0 stable docs; release tag commit bb1d8e8.
sources.locator: ImageOps.exif_transpose() section.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Pillow stable API docs; confirmed version and transpose behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: If EXIF Orientation is present and not 1, transpose accordingly and remove orientation data; in_place defaults false.
sources.applicability: Candidate API; verify TIFF decoder behavior and original-image immutability in pinned release.

sources.title: Pillow ImageCms 12.3.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: Pillow 12.3.0 stable docs; release tag commit bb1d8e8.
sources.locator: profileToProfile() API and renderingIntent argument.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official API docs at transform function.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies ICC transform from inputProfile to outputProfile; rendering intent defaults to perceptual; invalid profiles or unsupported output modes raise PyCMSError.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit color conversion and profile-failure handling.

sources.title: Pillow Image limits
sources.released_version_or_commit: Pillow 12.3.0 stable docs; release tag commit bb1d8e8.
sources.locator: Decompression-bomb warning/error discussion near Image.open().
sources.observed_operation: Opened official docs and inspected warning/error threshold behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Above MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS emits DecompressionBombWarning; callers can promote to error; over twice the threshold raises DecompressionBombError. Threshold may be changed or disabled.
sources.applicability: Useful explicit guard behavior; component must set its own threshold.

sources.title: Pillow exif_transpose regression #5580 and fix #5584
sources.released_version_or_commit: Bug on Pillow 8.3.0; PR #5584 fix reported released in Pillow 8.3.1 (2021).
sources.locator: Issue reproduction, linked PR #5584 and maintainer comment reporting 8.3.1 fix.
sources.observed_operation: Read upstream issue and release-resolution comments.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Change intended to avoid EXIF mutation exposed KeyError when deleting orientation from alternate EXIF data; fix merged/released.
sources.applicability: Test decode/storage variants and unchanged original, not only visible rotation.

sources.title: Pillow TIFF YCbCr orientation issue and fix
sources.released_version_or_commit: PR #8556 merged 2025-03-29; release version not asserted in inspected PR.
sources.locator: PR description/comments linked to #8554; libtiff applies orientation during TIFFRGBAImage decode.
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream PR and read merge date, linked issue, and TIFF/libtiff explanation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For YCbCr TIFF, libtiff may apply orientation during decode; Pillow removes orientation metadata to prevent later double transpose.
sources.applicability: Decoder path and format matter; test pinned stack rather than assuming the application always owns orientation.

sources.title: ImageMagick command-line options
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current online docs inspected 2026-10-12; latest changelog observed as 7.1.2-33.
sources.locator: -auto-orient, -profile, -strip, -limit and resource-limit discussion.
sources.observed_operation: Opened current command-option docs and located behavior for orientation, profiles, stripping and resources.

F-01.detail: Specify premultiplied-alpha filtering and unpremultiplication when alpha is nonzero as component policy; candidate behavior remains unverified. CSS Color Level 5 is a Working Draft about color interpolation, not a normative resize rule.

F-02.detail: Keep SRC-PNG-02 bound to the Second Edition; preserve CRITIC-PNG-01 and add separate REV-W3C-PNG-01 for Third Edition context.

F-03.detail: Add ITU-T T.86 V2 APPn inventory; require owner-selected formats and per-format encoded-output allowlist checks. Not exhaustive, and blanket APPn removal can discard ICC/color data.

F-04.detail: Atomic publication depends on actual destination/staging semantics; use confirmed same-filesystem rename, otherwise a commit-marker/state protocol. No behavior tested.

F-05.detail: Issue and linked patch commit corroborate chronology. Reporter describes regressions; maintainer says patch reverted as incorrect. No independent root cause or current-release behavior established.

sources.release_version_or_commit: Current Google for Developers format specification; no numbered version shown

sources.observed_operation: Extended WebP can carry ICCP, EXIF, XMP, alpha, animation frames and unknown chunks. ICCP is before image data; without ICCP, sRGB should be assumed. Metadata chunks may appear out of order; trailing data may be ignored by readers.

sources.applicability: Sanitized export should rebuild the RIFF container from pixels and keep only needed alpha/target ICC and animation data; test duplicate, unknown and trailing chunks if accepting WebP.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.version_or_commit: Current official documentation; no page release version displayed

sources.observed_operation: Read the documentation describing backup from a live SQLite database.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A completed call sequence creates a bitwise-identical snapshot of the source at backup start. Other connections may write while a backup proceeds; external writes can force restart, and repeated restarts can prevent completion. Online Backup API copies a database into another database, not arbitrary app files.
sources.applicability: Use if the eventual workspace has SQLite; it informs safe database capture but does not settle consistency with attachments/preferences.

sources.locator: Section 4, The WAL File
sources.observed_operation: Read the official description of the database WAL file lifecycle and persistent state.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: While connections are open in WAL mode there is a companion -wal file. It is normally deleted after clean last close, but may persist after unclean exit or persistent-WAL configuration. The WAL is part of persistent database state and should be kept with a copied/moved database; separating them may lose committed work or corrupt it.
sources.applicability: Applies to direct-copy approaches for a workspace database configured for WAL; motivates using SQLite backup APIs or a quiesced coordinated capture.
sources.limitations: This page is not an application-level snapshot protocol and says nothing about separate attachment files/preferences.

sources.locator: Section 1 Introduction; section 4 Rollback; section 5 Multi-file Commit

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The article says SQLite transactions appear atomic across the participating database change, including crash interruption, under the described mechanism; the walkthrough applies to rollback mode, with WAL treated separately. Multi-file commit through ATTACH is a distinct mechanism, not a transaction over arbitrary filesystem resources.
sources.applicability: Use to bound claims about database transaction atomicity and to motivate a separate app-level commit boundary for resources/preferences.
sources.limitations: It does not establish a cross-platform atomic swap of a mixed database/files workspace or durability on every filesystem/device.

reviser_review.observed_operation: Opened W3C WebVTT specification and checked cue timing rules: starts are nondecreasing, each end exceeds its start, and intervals may overlap. This defines track-relative offsets, not binding to an audio byte revision.

reviser_review.applicability: Use cue times only when the application binds that exact transcript revision to an exact audio revision; binding is provenance, not proof of accuracy/synchronization.

sources.title: Loro JavaScript API Reference

sources.locator: LoroTree methods createNode/move/delete/getNodeByID/isNodeDeleted; TreeID and event types; API reference tree notes
sources.observed_operation: Provides stable TreeID-based create/move/delete access, a deleted-state query, movable list operations, and concurrent-move cycle prevention. API warns tree fractional indexing can interleave under concurrent insertions while preserving order.

sources.title: Loro Tree tutorial

sources.locator: Events section and node retrieval examples
sources.observed_operation: Tree diffs carry create/move/delete actions and old/new parent/index; event order follows causality; delete event represents target plus subtree and does not emit child-specific delete events.

sources.applicability: Useful for grouping/ungrouping event interpretation, but group membership alone cannot determine whether a thread should move to a group or remain on its original child.

sources.title: Loro shallow snapshots
sources.released_version_or_commit: Loro 1.0 feature; current docs
sources.locator: Basic Usage, Content Redaction, Synchronization Limitations, Archive and Trim
sources.observed_operation: Shallow snapshot encodes current state while trimming operations before a chosen frontier; docs give a typical 70–90% size reduction and show removal of sensitive deleted text from the new snapshot.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Peers can sync only if they are based after the shallow snapshot point; all peers must receive the sanitized document for old content to be removed everywhere. Archiving full history preserves data that trimming was intended to remove.
sources.applicability: Demonstrates that history retention, storage growth, sync cutoffs, and privacy are coupled decisions; keep compact comment-context snapshots separately and disclose retention/archives.

sources.title: Automerge conflict documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling current docs; release month Aug 2026 reports Automerge 3.4.1, but this page does not pin a package build
sources.locator: What is a Conflict; `Automerge.getConflicts`; operation ID ordering
sources.observed_operation: Concurrent writes to the same property expose a deterministic winner and keep alternatives accessible through conflict inspection; a later assignment resolves the conflict. Winner ordering uses operation ID, not wall-clock time.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A deterministic winner is convergence behavior, not a judgment that a comment target or layout intent is semantically correct. Reading the ordinary property view can hide a concurrent alternative unless the app inspects conflicts.
sources.applicability: Preserve conflict alternatives and provenance for consequential anchor resolution; do not convert a mechanical winner into silent reattachment.

sources.title: Automerge merge rules
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling current docs, not version-pinned
sources.locator: Map merge rules and list merge rules
sources.observed_operation: Documents concurrent map delete versus concurrent set as retaining the newly set value; list operations reference element IDs rather than raw numeric indices; concurrent insert/delete/update cases have explicit CRDT rules.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A concurrent set may make a map key visible again under the documented rule. It does not encode a product-level decision to undo a deliberate deletion or restore a user-visible object.
sources.applicability: Keep “layout replica convergence” separate from “review intent”; use application-level deletion/tombstone state and explicit undo/restore events.

sources.title: Automerge repository storage
sources.released_version_or_commit: Automerge Repo current docs; page not package-version pinned
sources.locator: Storage model; snapshots, incrementals, concurrent compaction
sources.observed_operation: Repo stores incremental changes and periodically compacts them into snapshots; concurrent compaction deletes only changes already incorporated, using document heads in snapshot identity.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is repo storage behavior, not Automerge core conflict semantics. Compaction preserves mergeable state/history according to the repo storage scheme; it is not user-visible comment retention policy.
sources.applicability: A useful storage option, but application-level tombstones, anchor context, and export retention still need a bounded policy.

sources.title: Automerge glossary: history compaction
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling current docs, not version-pinned
sources.locator: Compaction definition and tradeoffs
sources.observed_operation: Defines compaction as serializing current state without full history and notes it may be used for bandwidth/device constraints or to purge sensitive deleted content.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: After history compaction, the document may no longer sync with another replica that lacks a common ancestor. Purging one copy does not prove replicas/archives have also discarded content.
sources.applicability: Retention/privacy decisions must specify replica cutover, archive policy, and behavior for stale offline peers.

sources.title: Excalidraw reconcileElements implementation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Mutable `master` at access; no immutable commit hash exposed in browser response; public issue R17 says 0.18.1 for separate reported case
sources.locator: `shouldDiscardRemoteElement`, lines 456–497; `reconcileElements`, lines 547–619
sources.observed_operation: Reconciliation matches by element ID, discards a remote copy when the local item is being edited or has a greater version, and breaks equal-version ties with the lower versionNonce; it appends unmatched local elements, then orders/heals indices.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is one library’s record-version protocol, not a general merge law. An absent remote record does not by itself remove the local record in this function; deletion needs an explicit record/version state in the caller’s data.
sources.applicability: Concrete whiteboard caller/test surface to study; use as comparative behavior and regression-test inspiration, not as the proposal’s selected merge engine.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: Controlling Text Search
sources.version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 documentation; page reports 18 as current stable and 19 as development/beta at access
sources.locator: §12.3.1 document/query parsing; §12.3.3 ranking; tsvector, setweight, ts_rank, ts_rank_cd; lines 18-48 and 160-181
sources.observed_operation: Opened exact versioned URL via browser tooling; read page text and section locators
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Text vectors use selected/default text-search configuration; dictionaries normalize/stem or discard stop words; title/body weights are caller-assigned; ranking docs describe relevance as application-specific; default rank weights are {0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 1.0}.
sources.applicability: Primary lexical alternative; explains exact token and ranking behavior. Not semantic search, access control, or a calibrated authority/confidence score.
sources.evidence_summary: Postgres FTS parses to tsvector and ranks using lexical, proximity, and structural signals; rank is application-specific.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: GIN Indexes
sources.version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 documentation
sources.locator: §65.4 introduction and §65.4.5 gin_fuzzy_search_limit
sources.observed_operation: Opened exact versioned URL and followed find for full-text search
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: GIN supports inverted lookup including document lexemes; gin_fuzzy_search_limit defaults to 0 (no limit); nonzero returns a soft, random subset, not a top-ranked truncation.
sources.applicability: Supports lexical FTS and an important completeness caveat if the non-default fuzzy limit is enabled.
sources.evidence_summary: GIN is an inverted index for composite values such as documents; a nonzero soft limit is not deterministic ranking.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: Row Security Policies
sources.version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 documentation
sources.locator: §5.9 opening behavior, owner/superuser bypass, policy composition
sources.observed_operation: Opened exact versioned URL and read policy conditions
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: RLS must be enabled; with no policies behavior is default-deny. Table owners normally bypass; superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass. Multiple permissive policies combine with OR; restrictive policies with AND. TRUNCATE and REFERENCES are outside RLS.
sources.applicability: Authorization alternative if content and search rows are in PostgreSQL; app connections must not run as privileged owner/bypass roles and all read paths need review.
sources.evidence_summary: RLS is a row-query boundary with explicit privilege and command exceptions, not a generic cache or citation policy.

sources.title: SQLite Transaction
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Transactions, read versus write, default DEFERRED behavior, and busy commit conditions.
sources.observed_operation: Official SQLite page opened and transaction semantics read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: SQLite permits multiple readers but only one simultaneous writer; commit can return SQLITE_BUSY. A single transaction groups DB changes.
sources.applicability: Coordinate run-state and search-index changes in transactions while handling busy/retry behavior; database atomicity does not make filesystem deletion safe.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Introduction and rollback-journal atomic commit scope.
sources.observed_operation: Official SQLite technical note opened.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Explains atomic transaction property for a single database file, specifically rollback-journal mode; WAL has separate documentation.
sources.applicability: Database metadata transitions may be transactional, but an artifact file and the DB row need a deliberate publish/reconcile protocol.

sources.title: Accessing files from the macOS App Sandbox
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple developer documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Overview; security-scoped URL lifetime and startAccessingSecurityScopedResource / stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource.
sources.observed_operation: Official documentation search excerpt read; page open exposes JavaScript limitation but provided Markdown excerpt.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: User-selected URLs extend app access; security-scoped access must be started and stopped; file ACL/MAC controls may still deny.
sources.applicability: A broad notebook folder grant is too broad for one attachment; avoid passing reusable security-scoped roots into an extension.

sources.title: Process | Foundation
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple Foundation documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Sandbox note on child processes and XPC alternatives.
sources.observed_operation: Official search excerpt read; page open requires JavaScript.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A child launched by Process inside a sandboxed app inherits the parent's sandbox; different helper entitlements require XPC services.
sources.applicability: A plain spawned child is not a per-extension permission sandbox on macOS.

sources.title: XPC | Apple Developer Documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple XPC documentation accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Overview and service type table; privilege isolation, process lifetime, on-demand launch/restart.
sources.observed_operation: Official Apple developer search excerpt read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: XPC services are separate processes; an XPC service per client is tied to the client lifetime. Different service types carry different user/root context.
sources.applicability: Potential macOS containment implementation; configure minimal service entitlements and narrow IPC rather than passing notebook access.

sources.title: AppContainer isolation - Win32 apps
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn documentation; AppContainer feature introduced in Windows 8.
sources.locator: File, network, process isolation; capability grants.
sources.observed_operation: Official Microsoft Learn search result inspected.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Resources are isolated by default with specific capabilities granted as needed; user/application identities and ACLs also govern access.
sources.applicability: Candidate Windows sandbox primitive; validate packaged/unpackaged launch support and each requested capability on supported Windows versions.

sources.title: Job Objects - Win32 apps
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn documentation retrieved 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Managing processes in jobs, job limits, process-tree limitations and breakaway flags.
sources.observed_operation: Official page opened; process inheritance, limits, and tree management sections read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Children created with CreateProcess join by default, but breakaway flags/settings and some process creation paths bypass the job. Nested jobs require Windows 8+.
sources.applicability: Use for process-tree CPU/memory/time/termination only with breakaway disabled or explicitly handled and tested.

sources.title: Control Group v2 — Linux Kernel documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Linux kernel v6.6 documentation.
sources.locator: Memory and CPU controllers, including memory.max and cpu.max.
sources.observed_operation: Official kernel documentation search result read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Cgroup controls account/limit process-group resource use; kernel documents possible over/under reclaim around memory targets.
sources.applicability: Candidate Linux resource limits for whole worker tree; requires cgroup delegation/permissions and runtime support checks.

sources.title: seccomp(2) — Linux manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Current Linux man-pages documentation retrieved 2026-10-12; kernel feature details are version-conditioned in the page.
sources.locator: Filter actions, thread synchronization flags, SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS.
sources.observed_operation: Linux man page search excerpt read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Filters constrain system calls; available flags/actions vary by kernel version and filters do not by themselves define filesystem/network namespace or CPU/memory budgets.
sources.applicability: One part of Linux defense-in-depth; feature-probe at runtime and pair with resource and filesystem controls.

sources.title: Filesystem sandbox escape when paths or symlinks contain trailing slashes
sources.version_or_commit: Advisory GHSA-vqjp-4c8c-hfgg, published 2026-08-20; patch versions 24.0.13, 36.0.14, 46.0.3, 47.0.4; 48.0.0+ reported unaffected.
sources.locator: Affected/patched versions, impact, Linux openat2 condition, patch/workaround.
sources.observed_operation: Official GitHub security advisory opened; affected versions and impact read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Trailing slash/symlink paths could escape WASI filesystem sandbox on affected releases; specific issue not present with Linux kernel >5.6 using openat2, while macOS/older Linux are affected.
sources.applicability: Requires patch/version monitoring and symlink/trailing-slash cross-platform regression tests; do not infer that capability APIs eliminate path bugs.

review_observation.observed_operation: Official primary page opened/inspected in the critic review; the entry’s original investigator evidence fields are preserved verbatim.

sources.title: Guest-controlled resource exhaustion in WASI implementations
sources.version_or_commit: Advisory published 2026-02-24; patch releases include 24.0.6, 36.0.6, 40.0.4, 41.0.4, 42.0.0.
sources.locator: Impact; WASIp1/WASIp2; host memory, handles, I/O buffers; default limit behavior by release.
sources.observed_operation: Official advisory opened; affected versions, host API pathways, patch caveat read.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Guest-controlled host allocations/buffering could exhaust memory or crash; older patched stable branches kept limits very large by default; 42.0.0+ defaults were tuned to avoid the reported issue.
sources.applicability: Bound host-call data, buffers, handles, output, and disk separately; runtime patch alone may not select safe embedder quotas.

review_observation.observed_operation: Official primary page opened/inspected in the critic review; the entry’s original investigator evidence fields are preserved verbatim.

sources.title: Excessive allocated memory on the host when guests don't have stdio
sources.version_or_commit: GHSA-gqmc-89g8-p25r, published 2026-10-02; patched in Wasmtime 36.0.17, 48.0.4, 49.0.2.
sources.locator: Affected versions and patches; Impact; workaround; WASI Preview 2 SinkOutputStream, write-zeroes and stdout/stderr configuration (captured page lines 139–158).
sources.observed_operation: Official GitHub security advisory opened; full affected ranges, condition, patch list and bounded OutputStream workaround inspected.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The wasmtime-wasi WASI Preview 2 SinkOutputStream used by default when stdout/stderr are unconfigured failed to limit a write-zeroes allocation. Affected: <36.0.17, 37.0.0–48.0.3, 49.0.0–49.0.1. Patched: 36.0.17, 48.0.4, 49.0.2. Configured stdout/stderr streams typically have limits; custom OutputStream with bounded check_write is a workaround.
sources.applicability: Only applies to embeddings without configured stdout/stderr using the affected wasmtime-wasi paths; require bounded output streams and test this default explicitly if Wasmtime/WASIp2 is selected.
